--- ## title: "Converted Presentation" format: revealjs: theme: default pagetitle: 'Spatial capture-recapture I' slide-number: true echo: true lang: en --- ## {content-align="center" style="font-size: 150%;"}
**Spatial capture-recapture for
closed populations**
::: {style='font-size: 60%;'} WILD(FISH) 8390
Inference for Models of Fish and Wildlife Population Dynamics
:::
# Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## [SCR overview -- Two motivations]{style='font-size: 85%;'} ::: {style='font-size: 65%;'} 1. Improved inference - Non-spatial models don't account for important sources of variation in $p$. * Distance between animals and traps * Trap-specific covariates - SCR makes it possible to estimate *density*, not just $N$ in an unknown region. 2. Improved science - We can ask new questions, such as: * What influences spatial variation in density? * How do survival and recruitment vary in space and time? * How does movement influence density and detectability?
::: {.fragment}
**Rather than think of SCR as a new estimation tool, you can think of it as an individual-based framework for inference on spatial population dynamics.**
::: ::: ## SCR data ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} SCR capture histories can be organized as a 3D array where $y_{ijk}$ indicates if individual $i=1,\dots,n$, was captured in trap $j=1,\dots,J$ on occasion $k=1,\dots,K$. ::: {style='font-size: 60%;'} +----------------+----------------------------------+ | | Occasion | +:===============+:==:+:==:+:==:+:==:+:==:+:==:+:==:+ | | Trap | | Trap | +----------------+--------------+----+--------------+ | | 1 | | 2 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ | Individual | 1 | 2 | 3 | | 1 | 2 | 3 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | 1 | 0 | 1 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | | 0 | 1 | 1 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 | | 0 | 0 | 0 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ | 4 | 0 | 1 | 1 | | 1 | 0 | 0 | +----------------+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ :::
::: {.fragment} Because we know the coordinates of the traps, we also know when and where each individual was detected. ::: ::: {.fragment} This spatial information has been available all along, but it wasn't utilized to estimate density until Efford (2004, Oikos). ::: ::: ## [Closed population model (*N* known hypothetically) ]{style="font-size: 60%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 50%;'} State model (a spatial point process model) $$ \lambda({\bf s}) = \exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 w_1({\bf s}) + \beta_2 w_2({\bf s}) + \cdots) \\ \Lambda = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \lambda({\bf s}) \; \mathrm{d}{\bf s} \\ N \sim \mathrm{Pois}(\Lambda) \\ {\bf s}_i \propto \lambda({\bf s}) \;\; \mathrm{for}\; i=1,\dots,N $$ Observation model (supposing $N$ was known) $$ p_{ij} = g_0\exp(-\|{\bf s}_i - {\bf x}_j\|^2/(2\sigma^2)) \;\; \mathrm{for}\, j=1,\dots,J \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_{ij}) $$ ::: ::: {style='font-size: 50%;'} $\lambda({\bf s})$ -- "Intensity function" describing expected density of individuals at location $\bf s$
$\Lambda$ -- Expected number of individuals in the spatial region $\mathcal{S}$
$N$ -- Realized number of individuals (ie, population size)
${\bf s}_i$ -- Location of the $i$th activity center
${\bf x}_j$ -- Location of trap $j$
$\|{\bf s}_i - {\bf x}_j\|$ -- Euclidean distance between ${\bf s}_i$ and ${\bf x}_j$
$g_0$ -- Capture probability when distance between activity centers and traps is 0
$\sigma$ -- Scale parameter of encounter function
$p_{ij}$ -- Capture probability
$y_{ijk}$ -- Spatial capture histories
::: ## [Closed population model (*N* known hypothetically)]{style="font-size: 60%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Many variations and extensions are possible for both the state and observation models, but today we will focus on the simplest case with no spatial variation in the expected value of density. ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} $$ N \sim \mathrm{Pois}(\lambda) \\ {\bf s}_i \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\cal S) \\ p_{ij} = g_0\exp\left(\frac{-\|{\bf s}_i - {\bf x}_j\|^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_{ij}) $$ :::
::: {.fragment} Just remember, this formulation isn't exactly correct because we can't observe the "all zero" encounter histories (and thus we don't know $N$). ::: ::: ## {.smaller}

# Simulation ## Homogeneous Poisson point process ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lambda1 <- 25; A <- 1 ## lambda1=density, A=area N <- rpois(1, lambda1*A) s <- cbind(runif(N, 0, 1), runif(N, 0, 1)) plot(s, pch=16, col="blue", xlab="Easting", ylab="Northing", xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), cex.lab=1.5, asp=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/ppp1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## Traps ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- cbind(rep(seq(0.15, 0.85, by=0.1), each=8), rep(seq(0.15, 0.85, by=0.1), times=8)) ## Trap locations plot(s, pch=16, col="blue", xlab="Easting", ylab="Northing", asp=1, main="Activity centers and traps") points(x, pch=3) ## Trap locations ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/traps1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## [Distance between traps and activity centers]{style="font-size: 80%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Compute distances between activity centers (${\bf s}_1, \dots, {\bf s}_N$) and traps (${\bf x}_1, \dots, {\bf x}_J$). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} J <- nrow(x) ## nTraps dist.sx <- matrix(NA, N, J) for(i in 1:N) { dist.sx[i,] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[,2])^2) } ``` ::: Look at distances between first 4 individuals and first 5 traps. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round(dist.sx[1:4,1:5], digits=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 0.88 0.85 0.82 0.81 0.81 [2,] 0.88 0.79 0.71 0.63 0.56 [3,] 0.27 0.33 0.41 0.50 0.59 [4,] 0.79 0.80 0.83 0.87 0.92 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Capture probability ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Compute capture probability ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g0 <- 0.2 sigma <- 0.05 p <- g0*exp(-dist.sx^2/(2*sigma^2)) ``` :::
Look at capture probs for first 4 individuals and first 5 traps. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round(p[1:4,1:5], digits=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 0 0 0 0 0 [2,] 0 0 0 0 0 [3,] 0 0 0 0 0 [4,] 0 0 0 0 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Capture histories ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Simulate capture histories for all $N$ individuals ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} K <- 5 # nOccasions y.all <- array(NA, c(N, J, K)) for(i in 1:N) { for(j in 1:J) { y.all[i,j,] <- rbinom(K, 1, prob=p[i,j]) } } ``` ::: Discard individuals not captured ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} captured <- rowSums(y.all)>0 y <- y.all[captured,,] ``` ::: Capture histories for first 2 individuals and first 5 traps on first occasion. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y[1:2,1:5,1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 0 0 0 0 0 [2,] 0 0 0 0 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Summary stats ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Individuals captured ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (n <- nrow(y)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 18 ``` ::: ::: Capture frequencies ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y.tilde <- rowSums(y) table(y.tilde) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` y.tilde 1 2 3 4 9 7 1 1 ``` ::: ::: Spatial recaptures ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y.nok <- apply(y, c(1, 2), sum) y.nojk <- apply(y.nok>0, 1, sum) table(y.nojk) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` y.nojk 1 2 3 13 4 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Spider plot ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/spider-1.png){fig-align='center' width=55%} ::: ::: ::: # Likelihood ## Software options - Program DENSITY * Windows program with GUI - R package 'secr' * The oldest R package with the most options - R package 'oSCR' * A newer R package with similar functionality ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Import data from two text files ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(secr) sch <- read.capthist(captfile="encounter_data_file.csv", trapfile="trap_data_file.csv", detector="proximity", fmt="trapID") summary(sch) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Object class capthist Detector type proximity Detector number 64 Average spacing 100 m x-range 150 850 m y-range 150 850 m Counts by occasion 1 2 3 4 5 Total n 9 4 4 6 6 29 u 9 1 2 3 3 18 f 9 7 2 0 0 18 M(t+1) 9 10 12 15 18 18 losses 0 0 0 0 0 0 detections 9 5 4 6 6 30 detectors visited 9 5 4 6 6 30 detectors used 64 64 64 64 64 320 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(sch) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/secr-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Fit the SCR equivalent of Model $M_0$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm.M0 <- secr.fit(sch, model=list(D=~1, g0=~1, sigma=~1), details = list(fastproximity = FALSE), ## For AIC comparisons buffer=150, trace=FALSE, ncores=3) coef(fm.M0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` beta SE.beta lcl ucl D -1.050968 0.2738747 -1.587753 -0.5141834 g0 -1.276753 0.4489717 -2.156721 -0.3967843 sigma 3.789683 0.1342465 3.526565 4.0528010 ``` ::: ::: Estimates on original scale ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fm.M0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3495992 0.09757018 0.2043844 0.5979887 g0 logit 0.2181035 0.07656510 0.1037048 0.4020852 sigma log 44.2423619 5.96624128 34.0069365 57.5584511 ``` ::: :::
`D` is density ($\lambda$, animals/ha), `g0` is $g_0$, and `sigma` is $\sigma$.
::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Fit the SCR equivalent of Model $M_t$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm.Mt <- secr.fit(sch, model=list(D=~1, g0=~t, sigma=~1), buffer=150, trace=FALSE, ncores=3) coef(fm.Mt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` beta SE.beta lcl ucl D -1.0603936 0.2725340 -1.594550 -0.5262367 g0 -0.6434653 0.6623739 -1.941694 0.6547637 g0.t2 -0.8125256 0.7056696 -2.195613 0.5705614 g0.t3 -1.1182751 0.7397397 -2.568138 0.3315881 g0.t4 -0.6023297 0.6829484 -1.940884 0.7362246 g0.t5 -0.6045682 0.6819724 -1.941210 0.7320733 sigma 3.7799754 0.1330984 3.519107 4.0408435 ``` ::: ::: Estimates on original scale ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fm.Mt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3463195 0.09616385 0.2029998 0.5908242 g0 logit 0.3444636 0.14956962 0.1254618 0.6580832 sigma log 43.8149643 5.85762566 33.7542824 56.8742975 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Fit the SCR equivalent of Model $M_b$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm.Mb <- secr.fit(sch, model=list(D=~1, g0=~b, sigma=~1), buffer=150, trace=FALSE, ncores=3) coef(fm.Mb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` beta SE.beta lcl ucl D -0.9355618 0.5587887 -2.030768 0.1596439 g0 -1.5401416 1.0918175 -3.680065 0.5997815 g0.bTRUE 0.2900354 1.0711536 -1.809387 2.3894579 sigma 3.7945281 0.1361532 3.527673 4.0613835 ``` ::: ::: Estimates on original scale ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fm.Mb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3923654 0.2375315 0.13123476 1.1730930 g0 logit 0.1765147 0.1587036 0.02460088 0.6456063 sigma log 44.4572512 6.0811580 34.04464338 58.0545716 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 75%;'} What about $N$? `E.N` is the expected value of $N$. `R.N` is the realized value of $N$. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region.N(fm.M0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl n E.N 34.24296 9.556923 20.01929 58.57253 18 R.N 34.24297 7.555912 24.82226 56.67252 18 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region.N(fm.Mt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl n E.N 33.92172 9.419174 19.88367 57.87077 18 R.N 33.92173 7.402642 24.69007 55.89223 18 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region.N(fm.Mb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl n E.N 38.43188 23.26603 12.85434 114.9035 18 R.N 38.43189 22.42490 21.57669 134.7173 18 ``` ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' Was `buffer` big enough? ::: {style='font-size: 75%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(update(fm.M0, buffer=100))[1,] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3554085 0.09872472 0.2082871 0.6064475 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(update(fm.M0, buffer=150))[1,] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.349599 0.09757013 0.2043843 0.5979884 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(update(fm.M0, buffer=200))[1,] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3494254 0.09755105 0.204251 0.5977846 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(update(fm.M0, buffer=250))[1,] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3494237 0.09755102 0.2042495 0.5977831 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(update(fm.M0, buffer=300))[1,] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.3494236 0.097551 0.2042495 0.5977829 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' AIC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} AIC(fm.M0, fm.Mt, fm.Mb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model detectfn npar logLik AIC AICc dAIC AICwt fm.M0 D~1 g0~1 sigma~1 halfnormal 3 -117.3269 240.654 242.368 0.000 0.6867 fm.Mb D~1 g0~b sigma~1 halfnormal 4 -117.2848 242.570 245.646 1.916 0.2635 fm.Mt D~1 g0~t sigma~1 halfnormal 7 -115.9497 245.899 257.099 5.245 0.0499 ``` ::: ::: # Data augmentation ## Data augmentation model The DA version of a basic SCR model is: ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} $$ {\bf s}_i \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\mathcal{S}) \\ z_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi) \\ p_{ij} = g_0\exp\left(\frac{-\|{\bf s}_i-{\bf x}_j\|^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_i \times p_{ij}) \\ N=\sum_{i=1}^M z_i $$ ::: ## Model SCR~0~ -- data augmentation
[SCR0.jag](SCR0.jag)
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { g0 ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Baseline capture probability sigma ~ dunif(0, 0.5) ## Scale parameter of encounter function psi ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Data augmentation parameter for(i in 1:M) { s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1], xlim[2]) ## x-coord of activity center s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1], ylim[2]) ## y-coord of activity center z[i] ~ dbern(psi) ## Is individual real? for(j in 1:J) { dist[i,j] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[j,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[j,2])^2) p[i,j] <- g0*exp(-dist[i,j]^2/(2*sigma^2)) for(k in 1:K) { y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(z[i]*p[i,j]) ## Model for the capture histories } } } EN <- M*psi ## Expected value of N N <- sum(z) ## Realized value of N } ``` ::: ::: ## Model SCR~0~ -- data augmentation ::: {style='font-size: 75%;'} Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} M <- 150 y.aug <- array(0, c(M, J, K)) y.aug[1:nrow(y),,] <- y jags.data.SCR0 <- list(y=y.aug, M=M, J=J, K=K, x=x, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1)) ``` ::: Inits and parameters ::: {.cell report='false'} ```{.r .cell-code} ji.SCR0 <- function() { si <- cbind(runif(M), runif(M)) for(i in 1:nrow(y)) { traps_with_dets_i <- rowSums(y[i,,]>0) si[i,] <- colMeans(x[traps_with_dets_i,,drop=FALSE]) } list(z=rep(1,M), psi=runif(1), s=si, g0=runif(1), sigma=runif(1, 0.05, 0.1)) } jp.SCR0 <- c("g0", "sigma", "EN", "N") ``` ::: MCMC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.post.SCR0 <- jags.basic(data=jags.data.SCR0, inits=ji.SCR0, parameters.to.save=jp.SCR0, model.file="SCR0.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.burnin=0, n.iter=2000, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: ::: ## Posterior summaries ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(jags.post.SCR0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Iterations = 101:2100 Thinning interval = 1 Number of chains = 3 Sample size per chain = 2000 1. Empirical mean and standard deviation for each variable, plus standard error of the mean: Mean SD Naive SE Time-series SE EN 37.73026 10.232163 1.321e-01 0.4117271 N 37.30900 8.852848 1.143e-01 0.3695890 g0 0.22109 0.079680 1.029e-03 0.0036654 sigma 0.04543 0.006883 8.886e-05 0.0003373 2. Quantiles for each variable: 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% EN 21.37830 30.2722 36.57724 43.80305 60.71610 N 24.00000 31.0000 36.00000 42.00000 58.00000 g0 0.09579 0.1636 0.21099 0.26980 0.40370 sigma 0.03457 0.0408 0.04465 0.04902 0.06126 ``` ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.SCR0[,jp.SCR0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/plot-mcmc-SCR0-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## [Easy tricks to speed up Bayesian inference]{style="font-size: 80%;"} - Treat $z_i=1$ as data for first $n$ individuals. - If there are no occasion-specific covariates, collapse data and use binomial instead of Bernoulli distribution. - Use a single zero for each augmented individual, instead of an array of zeros. Then compute probability of detecting an individual at least once. ## Model SCR~0~ -- data augmentation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} writeLines(readLines("SCR0-faster.jag")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { g0 ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Baseline capture probability sigma ~ dunif(0, 0.5) ## Scale parameter of encounter function psi ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Data augmentation parameter for(i in 1:M) { s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1], xlim[2]) s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1], ylim[2]) z[i] ~ dbern(psi) for(j in 1:J) { dist[i,j] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[j,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[j,2])^2) p[i,j] <- g0*exp(-dist[i,j]^2/(2*sigma^2)) } } for(i in 1:n) { ## Model for observed capture histories for(j in 1:J) { y.tilde[i,j] ~ dbinom(p[i,j], K) } } for(i in (n+1):M) { ## Model for augmented guys PrAtLeastOneCap[i] <- 1-prod(1-p[i,])^K zero[i] ~ dbern(PrAtLeastOneCap[i]*z[i]) } EN <- M*psi ## Expected value of N N <- sum(z) ## Realized value of N } ``` ::: ::: ## Model SCR~0~ -- faster ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y.tilde <- apply(y, c(1,2), sum) n <- nrow(y) jags.data.SCR0.faster <- list(y.tilde=y.tilde, n=n, M=M, J=J, z=c(rep(1, n), rep(NA, M-n)), K=K, zero=rep(0, M), x=x, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1)) ``` ::: Inits and parameters (same as before) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ji.SCR0.faster <- function() { list(z=c(rep(NA, n), rep(0,M-n)), psi=runif(1), s=cbind(runif(M), runif(M)), g0=runif(1), sigma=runif(1, 0.05, 0.1)) } ``` ::: MCMC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.post.SCR0.faster <- jags.basic(data=jags.data.SCR0.faster, inits=ji.SCR0.faster, parameters.to.save=jp.SCR0, model.file="SCR0-faster.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.burnin=0, n.iter=2000, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: ::: ## Posterior summaries ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(jags.post.SCR0.faster) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Iterations = 101:2100 Thinning interval = 1 Number of chains = 3 Sample size per chain = 2000 1. Quantiles for each variable: 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% EN 21.68437 30.56296 36.1399 42.89445 61.90485 N 24.00000 31.00000 36.0000 41.00000 58.00000 g0 0.10293 0.17150 0.2202 0.27316 0.40942 sigma 0.03483 0.04019 0.0438 0.04787 0.05908 ``` ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.SCR0.faster[,jp.SCR0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial_files/figure-revealjs/plot-mcmc-SCR0-faster-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: # Summary ## Alternative observation models Common options include: ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Model Detector/Trap Examples ------------------------- --------------- -------------------- Bernoulli Proximity Hair-snares Poisson Count Camera trap Multinomial/Categorical Multi-catch Mist net, crab pot --- Single-catch Sherman trap :::
::: {.fragment} There are other observation models for data from area searches, transects, or acoustic recording units. ::: ## SCR study design ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
SCR involves model-based, rather than design-based, inference (see Ch. 10).
::: {.fragment} Random placement of traps is not required, but it's a good idea to randomly sample locations along the environmental gradients you're interested in. :::
::: {.fragment} The other two key design considerations are: - Capture as many individuals as you can (i.e., maximize $n$) - Obtain as many *spatial* recaptures as possible :::
::: {.fragment} There is a tradeoff between these two objectives. Simulation is often the best option for finding the right balance. ::: ::: ## SCR summary
We assume that variation in $p$ arises from distance between animals and traps.
We can estimate abundance and model distribution (i.e., spatial variation in density)
Next time, we'll see how to do that using secr and JAGS, and we'll make a bunch of maps. ## Assignment ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
